title: fix(lint): add the `_tabs` leg to validate-translation-references, and pin the object branch against the schema
body:
Fixes #13835

`validate-translation-references` walked the object branch's `fields`, `fields.*.options`, `_views`, `_sections` and `_actions`, and never `_tabs` — the string did not occur anywhere in the rule. **Premise re-verified on this branch before writing anything:** `grep -c '_tabs'` on the rule file returned **0** (grep exit 1), with a known-present control `grep -c '_sections'` on the same file returning **9**.

The defect is an **asymmetry**, not a coverage gap. `collectExpectedEntries` already emits `objects.OBJECT._tabs.TAB.label` and `os i18n check` demands a translation for it, while nothing told an author that a `_tabs` key they wrote names a filter preset that no longer exists. Rename a preset and the bundle keeps its old key: the tab bar renders in the source locale above a fully localized grid, with every gate green. Same shape as #11608's `flows` leg, one group over.

## What landed

**The leg.** `ObjectFacts` gains a `tabs` set; the object branch reports `translation-target-unknown` for a `_tabs` key no page declares, beside `_sections`, with the usual near-miss suggestion and an enumeration of the real preset names.

**The universe.** Collected from `page.interfaceConfig.userFilters.tabs[].name`, de-duplicated per object, mirroring `walkObjectTabs` in `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts` rather than re-deriving it — that file is untouched. Three shape facts were asked of the code that owns them rather than assumed, and each is pinned by a test:

- **`ViewTabSchema` has two carriers and only one is live.** `UserFiltersSchema.tabs` (the page-only preset bar, ADR-0047) is what objectui's `TabFilters` draws and what `translateInterfaceTabs` resolves; `ListViewSchema.tabs` has no renderer in either repo. Registering the dead carrier would make legal a key nothing resolves — the mirror image of the orphan this rule reports. The hint says so explicitly when an object declares no preset bar, because otherwise an author reads the finding as a bug in the rule and "fixes" it by moving the tab onto a list view.
- **The object binds through `interfaceConfig.source` first, then the page's own `object`** — the order both the resolver and the extractor use. A page-level lookup alone would file every `source`-bound list page's presets under the wrong object and report correct keys.
- **Source-authored pages (`kind` of `html` / `react` / `jsx`) are read here**, unlike in the component walk that skips their derived `regions` cache: `interfaceConfig` is authored metadata at the page root, and neither consumer consults `kind`.

**The coverage pin** (the hardening the issue proposed and triage elevated) — delivered, and it was cheap: `@objectstack/spec` is already a runtime dependency of `@objectstack/lint` and `ObjectTranslationDataSchema.shape` reads straight through the lazy-schema proxy, so **no new dependency edge and no spec change**. A ledger classifies every key the schema declares as either reference-checked or leaf copy; one assertion holds its key set equal to the schema's, so a new group fails here rather than shipping demanded-but-unchecked. The classification is not self-certifying: every `reference-checked` entry carries a bundle naming something the stack does not declare, and a second assertion requires that bundle to actually produce a finding — so claiming coverage costs a working leg, and the only cheap route is `leaf-copy`, which must state a reason and is a reviewable act.

## Verification

All readings below are from the final commit `b6776129`, and the working tree was clean (`git status --porcelain` empty) for every one of them.

**Reverse verification — direction predicted RED, observed RED.** The fix was committed *first*, so the restore leg pointed at a `HEAD` that really carried the implementation. The `_tabs` sub-walk was deleted and the mutation proven on disk against the text it targeted — the leg marker `facts.tabs.has(tabName)` went 1 to 0 and the file went 58042 to 56263 bytes — before anything was measured. Result: **7 failed, 52 passed**. No rebuild leg was owed and that is proven rather than assumed: the suite imports the rule by a **relative source specifier** (`./validate-translation-references.js`), so vitest resolves the `.ts` source and no `dist/` sits in the path.

The failures are exactly the reporting legs — the six `_tabs` cases plus the pin's "backs every reference-checked claim with a leg that actually reports". The *accepting* cases stayed green throughout, which is the point: without the leg the rule is silent in **both** directions, so "orphan reported" alone would not distinguish this fix from a rule that reports everything. The restore was verified byte-identical to `HEAD` (`git diff HEAD` empty, `git hash-object` equal to the `HEAD` blob `3b7c91b2`), not by an exit code. The script carried a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` restore on absolute paths.

**Green:**

| reading | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/validate-translation-references.test.ts` | 59 passed |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` (whole package) | 88 files, **2465 passed**, 5 skipped |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` | exit 0 — **but see the caveat below** |
| derived gate family, **30 of 33** commands | every one exit 0 (the other 3 are NOT MEASURED, below) |

The family was derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no hand-built path list), which named **29 families plus the convention-triggered set for editing a test file** — wider than the dispatch's own clue list. All ran green, including `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:where-matcher`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:type-check-coverage` and `check:type-source-resolution`. Exit codes were captured by redirecting first and reading `$?` before any pipe.

**Three of the 33 are NOT MEASURED locally — recorded as such, none is a red:**

- `check-test-completeness.mjs` exited **3**, printing its own "the local reading for this gate is NOT MEASURED ... it is not a red, and there is nothing here to fix" — it parses a saved test-run log that CI tees and a bare local invocation cannot produce.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited **3** with its own `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — this gate reads built output, and some package has no dist/`. Its subject is export maps and built output; this diff changes neither.
- `check:type-check-debt` needs the whole workspace closure built. That build was attempted **twice** in the foreground and hit the container's ~10-minute cap both times (`exit 124`), so it is left to CI. Evidence the diff does not move it: the ledger records **16** errors for `@objectstack/lint`, itemized across five test files, and `validate-translation-references.test.ts` is not among them; an ad-hoc tsc over the package's test files attributed **zero** errors to the added code.

**A measurement caveat worth stating plainly:** `packages/lint`'s `tsconfig.json` **excludes** `**/*.test.ts`, and the package is not onboarded to `check:test-typecheck`. So the green `typecheck` above is a true statement that says **nothing** about the test file this PR edits — it is NOT MEASURED, not green. Confirmed by `tsc --listFiles`, which counted the file **0** times. That is pre-existing state and out of scope here; it is already on record as its own issue (cited under Scope) rather than fixed as a rider.

## Scope

Advisory-only, as the whole rule is: findings are warnings, nothing new is refused at publish, no public surface widens, and no bundle that resolved before reports now. Changeset: `@objectstack/lint` patch. `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts` and `packages/spec` were read as references and are untouched.

The measurement caveat above was already on record before this card: #14173 covers it exactly (`packages/lint` has no tsc program that compiles its tests). Re-confirmed on this branch rather than re-filed, so no duplicate was created. #14173 is not addressed here and remains open.
